headline: Champion Pumpkin Grower Sets Sights on World Record
meta_description: Minnesota horticulture teacher Travis Gienger won his fifth giant pumpkin contest with a 2,389-pound gourd, now pursuing the world record.
summary_short: After winning his fifth US giant pumpkin contest, Travis Gienger is chasing the world record held by a 2,857-pound squash grown in England.
body:
Travis Gienger, a horticulture teacher from Minnesota, has won his fifth giant pumpkin contest—and now he's hungry for something bigger. He hauled his prize-winning gourd all the way to Half Moon Bay, California, for the annual weighing event, where his entry tipped the scales at an impressive 2,389 pounds. The victory was decisive, but what really has Gienger's attention is a record that slipped through his hands: the world title, currently held by a 2,857-pound squash grown on England's south coast just last week.

What makes this story more than just another competition triumph is Gienger's history with the record itself. As a previous world-record holder, he knows exactly what it takes to reach the peak of giant gourd growing. That experience fuels his determination now—he's not simply celebrating his latest win, but already focused on the challenge ahead of reclaiming the title he once held.

The competitive world of giant pumpkins and squashes reveals something quietly compelling about human ambition: the drive to push boundaries, even in the most unexpected corners of achievement. For Gienger, each contest is a step toward mastery, and each season brings new opportunity to prove that lightning can strike twice.

Event held in Half Moon Bay, California
